THE PINNACLE DEVELOPMENTAL JOURNEY

From present abilities
toward a wonderful life.

Section link

Pinnacle’s purpose is to help children grow toward self-sufficiency and participation in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations each child needs. The practical question is: “What can my child do now, what support will help next, and how will we understand progress?”

Share thisWhatsAppX

COMPANY-DESCRIBED LEVELS OF DETAIL

17 domains. 79 abilities. 349 skills.

A broad view of development, organised into abilities and skills that can inform a child-specific plan. The direction is practical: what helps this child communicate, learn, manage daily routines and take part in life?

  1. 17

    Developmental domains

    The broad areas considered in Pinnacle’s framework.

  2. 79

    Abilities

    The capabilities the framework helps organise.

  3. 349

    Skills

    More detailed skills to connect with individual goals.

591 observations · AbilityScore® 0–1000

The company-described observation framework and score support a starting point and subsequent progress review. A child’s plan selects relevant priorities; the totals do not mean every child needs every intervention.

Pinnacle-defined architecture: company walkthrough, page 26; September handout, pages 5–6. The standards below supply classification and terminology; WHO does not define these numerical totals. An item-level domain–ability–skill crosswalk has not been independently audited in this review.

Company walkthrough · page 26September handout · pages 5–6How the international standards connect
Share thisWhatsAppX

Different starting points. Meaningful everyday goals.

Families may arrive with questions about autism, ADHD, communication, sensory processing, movement, learning or other developmental concerns. Pinnacle’s stated purpose centres on the capabilities that help each child grow toward self-sufficiency and participate in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations they need.

  • Communication and choice

    Express a need, make a choice and connect with other people.

  • Daily-life independence

    Build participation in familiar routines and practise useful daily-living skills.

  • Learning and belonging

    Take part in school, relationships and community with appropriate support.

These are examples of individual goals, not promised results. Professional assessment identifies the support appropriate to each child; diagnosis and medical care remain important where indicated. The licensed software’s scope is non-diagnostic developmental support for ages 0–12, not treatment of every condition.

Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion · BIS scopeAge range and non-diagnostic intended use
Share thisWhatsAppX

A family needs a connected journey.

A car needs its engine, steering and wheels to work together. In the same way, assessment, therapy, home practice and progress review need coordination. Families should not have to assemble that plan alone.

Pinnacle describes a shared developmental pathway around the child. Diagnostic information can matter for clinical care and access to support; the plan also needs to address communication, daily routines, learning, relationships and participation.

Company-described care modelModules named in the BIS scope
Share thisWhatsAppX

  1. AbilityScore® · 0–1000

    01 Understand the child’s abilities

    Begin with what the child can do, their interests and the everyday situations where support would help. Pinnacle describes 17 developmental domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills, supported by 591 observations and an AbilityScore on a 0–1000 scale. These are different layers of its developmental framework.

    For the family: A starting point the family and care team can discuss together.

    Company walkthrough, page 26; September handout, pages 5–6
    Share thisWhatsAppX

  2. Prognose® + personal development kernel

    02 Build a child-specific direction

    Connect the observed abilities with priorities, readiness goals and a plan for this child. The dossier describes a personal development kernel: a persistent child-specific record of measurements, responses to techniques, environment and history that informs subsequent recommendations.

    For the family: Clarity about what to work on next, why it matters and who will help.

    Evidence Dossier, pages 48–49; BIS schedule, page 2
    Share thisWhatsAppX

  3. TherapeuticAI® + human oversight

    03 Coordinate professional support

    Use the plan to coordinate appropriate therapies and intervention. Pinnacle describes practitioners, parents, caregivers and educators contributing to the programme; software supports professional judgement and shared goals.

    For the family: People working from an agreed direction across the child’s support team.

    September handout, pages 5–7; MD-5 intended use
    Share thisWhatsAppX

  4. Everyday Therapy™ · 7–9 techniques a day

    04 Make the plan part of everyday life

    The September handout describes 7–9 techniques selected for the child’s programme each day. Parents and other caregivers receive guidance for practice connected to the child’s current abilities and goals; the care team agrees what is appropriate.

    For the family: A practical way to carry support into home routines and other everyday settings.

    September handout, pages 5–7
    Share thisWhatsAppX

  5. Fusion Module · people in the loop

    05 Observe, track and correct

    Record how practice goes and bring observations from the family and professionals back into review. The BIS schedule names parent, family, caregiver, therapist and clinical tracking and correction through the Fusion Module.

    For the family: A plan that can respond when an activity, setting or support needs to change.

    BIS licence schedule, page 2
    Share thisWhatsAppX

  6. Monthly AbilityScore refresh + progress review

    06 Reassess and explain the trajectory

    Compare the child’s present abilities with their own earlier assessments and review the next priorities. The company walkthrough describes a monthly AbilityScore refresh; the Whitebook also describes monthly review. The care team should explain the schedule and any child-specific changes.

    For the family: An understandable record of change over time, connected to daily-life goals—not a judgement of the child’s worth.

    Company walkthrough, pages 35, 37; Whitebook, page 12
    Share thisWhatsAppX

  7. Readiness indexes + real-life goals

    07 Grow toward self-sufficiency and participation

    Work toward communication, daily living, learning, relationships and participation in school and community. The BIS scope names seven readiness indexes, including Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion. Continue reassessment and support as needs change.

    For the family: A wonderful life defined with the child and family, including the supports that make participation possible.

    BIS licence schedule, page 2
    Share thisWhatsAppX

Review → adapt → practise → reassess. Progress review feeds the next plan. The direction is growing capability and participation, with continuing human support.

This is Pinnacle’s documented developmental-support approach. PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 is a non-diagnostic Class B SaMD for ages 0–12 under the supplied MD-5. A programme, score or licence does not guarantee independence, school entry or a particular outcome. Inclusion is a right; it is not conditional on a score.

Measurement versions and review cadence

The company walkthrough labels 17 domains, 79 abilities, 349 skills and 591 observations as different layers. The September 2026 handout also describes 349 skills, 17 domains and 591 observations. The earlier Whitebook uses 344 skills across six domains. The dossier acknowledges architecture changes, but a complete crosswalk between versions was not supplied. Newer counts should not be attached retrospectively to validation of an older version.

A 0–1000 score is a company-described developmental measure. It is not a diagnosis, an IQ score, a credit score or a guarantee of future independence. Review the methods and limitations alongside the number.

PINNACLE AT A GLANCE

Measurement. A connected plan.
Support for everyday life.

Share thisWhatsAppX
Section link

Pinnacle Blooms Network is a brand of Bharath Healthcare Laboratories Private Limited. Pinnacle describes a seven-stage child-development pathway connecting ability measurement, child-specific planning, integrated support, parent-guided practice and progress review toward participation and growing independence.

The documented combination brings together non-diagnostic Class B developmental-support software, a BIS scope schedule naming connected software modules, and a centre network with individually traceable source records. These documents explain the approach and its scope; each child’s plan and outcomes remain individual.

PARENTS IN THE LICENSED INTENDED USE

Parents are explicitly included in the licensed intended use.

“The software is intended to assist parents, therapists, educators, and caregivers by providing developmental ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting, and adaptive therapy-plan support for children aged 0–12 years.”

MD-5 MFG/MD/2026/000248 · intended-use annexure · 21 April 2026

Bring guided developmental practice into everyday life. The licensed intended use names parents and caregivers alongside therapists and educators. Families have an explicit role in using the software’s developmental-support functions, with goals and guidance appropriate to their child.

Pinnacle’s Everyday Therapy programme and Fusion Module describe how that participation connects with daily practice, feedback and professional review. The BIS schedule names parent, family and caregiver tracking and correction as part of the connected developmental journey.

Read the MD-5 intended-use annexureRead the BIS connected-module scope
What this wording establishes

The intended use identifies whom the software assists and what it supports. It does not confer professional therapist credentials, register a home as a therapy centre or replace appropriate clinical care. A worldwide exclusivity claim is not established by these documents.

Share thisWhatsAppX
Share thisWhatsAppX

WORDS IN THE ORIGINAL BIS SCHEDULE

“for the full developmental lifecycle of children.”

The schedule names AbilityScore, Prognose®, the Everyday Therapy Programme through TherapeuticAI®, the Fusion tracking and correction module, and seven readiness indexes—including Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion.

This is the named quality-system and software-module scope. The MD-5 records the device’s four intended functions: ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting and adaptive therapy-plan support. Both documents retain their named software and premises. The MD-5 intended population is ages 0–12; individual outcomes remain subject to the child’s circumstances and support.

Read the full software and developmental-module scope

“Design, development, verification and validation, release, deployment, maintenance, technical support and post-market surveillance of Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), including Pinnacle AI GPT-OS™, and Developmental Support Software (Non-Diagnostic), including developmental ability mapping (Ability Score), prognostic engine Prognose®, Clinical Intervention Every Day Therapy Programme through Therapeutic AI®, Parent, Family, Caregiver, Therapist, Clinical Tracking and Correction Fusion Module, School Readiness, Speech Readiness, Motor Readiness, Study IQ Readiness, Behavior Readiness, Self Sufficiency Index, Mainstream Inclusion Index, 7 readiness indexing and associated digital developmental support modules for the full developmental lifecycle of children.”

2.7 billion+

Structured developmental records.
One child’s journey at a time.

Share thisWhatsAppX
Section link

Company-reported in the 7 September 2026 handout.
Counting basis: database rows/events · cutoff 17 July 2026.

See the dated metric and counting basis

A developmental journey you can follow.

Session entries, assessment observations, technique ratings and other platform events can preserve a record over time. The practical question is how that history helps the care team review your child’s plan.

Volume describes the size of the record system. Useful decisions also depend on data quality, consistent measurement, appropriate use and professional judgement.

This is not a count of unique children, independent clinical-trial observations or verified AI-training examples. A large count alone does not prove clinical effectiveness.
Why do some Pinnacle sources say 2.5 billion+ and others 2.7 billion+?

The July dossier used a 2.5 billion+ floor and retired earlier 2.7 billion wording. The September handout subsequently reports 2.7 billion+ observed row counts. The source review distinguishes the 2.5 billion floor assertion in limited assurance from the 2.7 billion factual row-count finding under agreed procedures. Those procedures do not provide an assurance opinion.

These are dated measures with different reporting roles. Neither should be described as an audited count of AI-training examples. Restricted practitioner reports are not republished here.

INTERNATIONAL LANGUAGE. PERSONAL GOALS.

Structured for understanding.

Section link

Four distinct standards help explain the architecture: health information, functioning and participation, interventions, and clinical terminology. Their value depends on how accurately they are implemented.

Share thisWhatsAppX

World Health Organization

ICD-11 · health information

A common classification and clinical terminology for recording, comparing and aggregating health information. It gives health-related records a consistent reference language.

Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICD-11 reference alignment; this does not make the software diagnostic.

WHO · International Classification of DiseasesPinnacle mapping claims · dossier pages 45–46, 84
Share thisWhatsAppX

World Health Organization

ICF · functioning and participation

A framework covering body functions and structures, activities, participation and environmental context. It helps keep daily life and the support needed to participate in view.

Pinnacle’s handout and dossier describe ICF mappings. The dossier’s b-code examples describe body functions; activity, participation and environment need their own relevant codes.

WHO · International Classification of Functioning, Disability and HealthPinnacle mapping claims · dossier pages 45–46, 84
Share thisWhatsAppX

World Health Organization

ICHI · health interventions

A classification for recording and analysing health interventions through their target, action and means. It can help describe what intervention is delivered in a consistent way.

Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICHI intervention coding within its architecture.

WHO · International Classification of Health InterventionsPinnacle mapping claims · dossier pages 45–46, 84
Share thisWhatsAppX

SNOMED International

SNOMED CT · clinical terminology

A detailed clinical terminology that represents information through concepts, descriptions and relationships. It supports consistent meaning in electronic clinical records.

Pinnacle’s dossier describes SNOMED CT terminology alignment. SNOMED International is the responsible organisation.

SNOMED International · What is SNOMED CT?Pinnacle mapping claims · dossier pages 45–46, 84
Share thisWhatsAppX

Pinnacle’s framework, connected to international languages

The Evidence Dossier describes mappings to ICD-11, ICF and ICHI, alongside SNOMED CT and LOINC terminology and HL7 FHIR representations. These are company-described architecture and mapping claims. Correctly implemented mappings can support more consistent records, exchange and analysis across settings.

The reviewed evidence does not include a complete item-by-item mapping audit or implementation-conformance report. Classification alignment does not establish WHO, UN or SNOMED endorsement, validate the developmental score, or expand the MD-5 intended use.

Evidence Dossier, pages 45–46, 84 and 86; September handout, pages 6 and 8WHO classification licence · use and endorsement

DESIGNED FOR WIDER REACH

A population-scale ambition. One child’s life at the centre.

Pinnacle describes a connected developmental-support architecture designed for wider deployment: a common framework, a persistent child-specific record, guided daily practice and human review. Its potential value at scale is continuity—helping families and professionals work from the same developmental direction across home, therapy and school.

What makes “sovereign-ready” and “world-ready” meaningful?

For a health system, sovereign readiness means demonstrable control over data and operations under its own governance requirements. International readiness also needs validated mappings, appropriate local language and workflows, applicable regulatory permissions, and evidence of safe, useful performance in that setting.

  • Local control and accountability

    Document hosting location, data-controller responsibilities, lawful use, consent, access controls and audit trails.

  • Interoperability in practice

    Validate the mappings and test information exchange with the systems that will actually use it.

  • Capacity and real-world value

    Test deployment performance, accessibility and child-centred outcomes in the intended population and setting.

The reviewed MD-5 and BIS scope establish specific regulatory and quality-system foundations. Reported network activity and information-security records add context. Together they support examining the deployment proposition; they are not a sovereign-grade certification or authorisation to operate in every country.

How to interpret reported data volume

The reported 2.7 billion+ structured records count database rows and events. They do not establish a nationally representative population, verified AI-training volume or population-level clinical effectiveness.

COMMON VERIFICATION QUESTIONS

Clear answers. Connected to the source.

Share thisWhatsAppX
Section link
What is PinnacleAI® GPT-OS licensed for?

The supplied MD-5 lists PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 as a Class B, non-diagnostic developmental-support device. Its scope is tied to the named device, version, intended use and premises; it does not establish diagnostic authority or guarantee clinical outcomes.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
Are an MD-3 application and an MD-5 licence the same?

No. MD-3 is an application for a manufacturing licence. MD-5 is the issued manufacturing licence. The original application is reviewed; Class B is recorded on the issued MD-5. The separate issued classification decision copy was not available for inspection.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
What do the BIS and ISO records establish?

They describe specified management systems and the activities and locations within their scope. They do not establish the effectiveness of every intervention or promise a particular outcome for a child.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
Does a research protocol prove external validation?

No. A protocol describes planned methods. The AbilityScore external-validation record here is a protocol; completed results and their limitations are needed before treating that study as completed validation.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
Does one credential cover every Pinnacle centre?

No. Match the named institution and premises on each document. This collection contains all 52 workbook centres and 53 distinct HFR identifiers across the workbook and certificate copies. Eight district summaries are separate; these are not counts of verified active centres.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
Who can help with a correction or a current document?

Contact Gokul Rao at care@pinnacleblooms.org or 9100 181 181. Include the record title, reference number and source date so the relevant document can be located.

Email the verification contact
Share thisWhatsAppX
What does Pinnacle’s 2.7 billion+ data-point figure mean?

The September 2026 company handout reports 2.7 billion+ structured platform records, based on database rows/events with a 17 July 2026 cutoff. Examples include session entries, assessment observations and technique ratings. The number is not a count of unique children, independent trial observations or verified AI-training examples.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
Does this establish the world’s largest child-development dataset?

No comparable worldwide ranking is established. For example, CentralReach reports over 5 billion clinical and financial data points, using a different counting basis. A valid comparison would need common definitions, dates, populations, data quality and permitted uses.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
Does the MD-5 licence approve the entire child-development lifecycle?

The MD-5 names PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 and defined non-diagnostic functions for ages 0–12. The broader BIS schedule lists software processes and developmental-support modules across the journey. These instruments establish different scopes; neither guarantees outcomes or certifies global exclusivity.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
Do WHO, UNICEF, CDC, NICE or UNESCO endorse Pinnacle?

No endorsement is established by the references on this page. Their guidance explains why monitoring, coordinated support, caregiver participation and inclusion matter. Pinnacle’s own documents must separately establish what Pinnacle provides.

Email the verification contact
Share thisWhatsAppX
What is the purpose of the Pinnacle developmental pathway?

Pinnacle’s purpose is to help children grow toward self-sufficiency and participation in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations each child needs. Its tagline is “Every child deserves a wonderful life.” The described approach connects ability measurement, child-specific planning, coordinated intervention, everyday practice, tracking, correction and reassessment. Individual outcomes vary.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
What do 17 domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills mean?

Pinnacle describes these as different layers of its developmental framework: 17 domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills, with 591 observations and AbilityScore on a 0–1000 scale. The totals belong to Pinnacle’s architecture, not a WHO-defined numerical hierarchy. Individual plans select relevant priorities. The earlier Whitebook used 344 skills across six domains; validation of an earlier version should not be automatically transferred to the newer framework.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
How do daily practice and monthly review connect?

The company sources describe 7–9 daily techniques selected for the child’s programme, human feedback through the Fusion tracking and correction module, and monthly AbilityScore refresh. The care team should explain the child-specific goals, practice guidance, review schedule and any adjustments. This is a programme description, not a guaranteed outcome.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
How do ICD-11, ICF, ICHI and SNOMED CT relate to PinnacleAI®?

Pinnacle’s dossier describes architecture and mappings using WHO’s ICD-11, ICF and ICHI, alongside SNOMED CT terminology from SNOMED International. Their roles are health information, functioning and participation, interventions, and consistent clinical meaning. Correct implementation can support interoperability; an item-by-item mapping audit was not supplied. Alignment is separate from endorsement, clinical validation and the licensed device’s intended use.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
Does Pinnacle focus on a diagnosis or on everyday-life goals?

Families may arrive with questions about autism, ADHD, communication, sensory processing, movement, learning or other developmental concerns. Pinnacle’s stated purpose centres on the capabilities that help each child grow toward self-sufficiency and participate in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations they need. These are examples of individual goals, not promised results. Professional assessment identifies the support appropriate to each child; diagnosis and medical care remain important where indicated. The licensed software’s scope is non-diagnostic developmental support for ages 0–12, not treatment of every condition.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
Is PinnacleAI® certified as sovereign-grade or authorised worldwide?

The reviewed documents do not establish a sovereign-grade certification or worldwide market authorisation. Pinnacle describes an architecture intended for population-scale developmental support. A specific deployment needs documented local control and governance, validated interoperability, applicable permissions, operational capacity and evidence of performance for that population. MD-5 and BIS provide the particular scopes shown in their records.

Read the evidence record
Share thisWhatsAppX
Are parents and caregivers named in the MD-5 intended use?

Yes. The MD-5 annexure states that PinnacleAI® GPT-OS is intended to assist parents, therapists, educators and caregivers through developmental ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting and adaptive therapy-plan support for ages 0–12. This explicitly includes family users of the licensed software. It does not confer professional therapist credentials or register homes as therapy centres; worldwide exclusivity has not been established.

A practical reading guide to the credentials, report types and international classifications used on this page. Each definition links to its Pinnacle source record.

SaMDSoftware as a Medical Device

Software intended for a medical purpose without being part of a hardware medical device. PinnacleAI® GPT-OS is listed as Class B, non-diagnostic developmental-support software in the supplied MD-5.

MD-3Application for a manufacturing licence

The application submitted for a licence to manufacture Class A or Class B medical devices. An application is a step in the regulatory record; it is not the issued licence.

Read the source record
MD-5Issued manufacturing licence

The issued licence records the named manufacturer, premises, device and intended use. Pinnacle’s supplied MD-5 names PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 for non-diagnostic developmental support, ages 0–12.

Read the source record
BIS scopeBureau of Indian Standards licence and scope schedule

The reviewed BIS record describes the management system and activities within its named scope, including developmental-support software modules. It does not establish every centre’s registration or guarantee clinical outcomes.

HFRHealth Facility Registry

The registry assigns a facility identifier. This page lists identifiers found in the supplied workbook and certificate copies. Source review is separate from confirming a facility’s current registry status, operational status or clinical quality.

An identifier for a practitioner’s document. The two supplied report numbers are recorded here; their particulars have not been independently matched on the ICAI portal in this review. A UDIN does not extend a report’s scope.
